category: infrastructure monitoring (hosted observability platform), programme for open source projects

free_tier.stated: Datadog at no cost for an open source project, applied for by form and evaluated case by case; the page publishes no amount, and the number of hosts (or other types of compute units) and telemetry events may be limited
free_tier.notes: The allowance is counted in hosts and telemetry events with no figure published; the vocabulary has no hosts unit, so the unit is mixed. The monitored infrastructure and applications must directly support the project. One recipient project reports using logs, metrics, APM and traces under the programme.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: the programme page names no payload limit

retention.stated: unverified: the programme page names no retention period

egress.terms: not stated: the programme page names no charge for reading data back

interface_detail: The Datadog API is an HTTP REST API; the programme page does not state whether the programme account includes API access
tooling: the Datadog web app and the Datadog REST API
chaining: For a project that meets the team conditions, Datadog at no cost for the infrastructure that runs the project; anyone else has the self-serve Free tier recorded as dev-services/datadog.

limits.value: the project must be non-commercial under an approved open source licence, at least 1 year old, with at least 5 regular contributors and at least 2 maintainers working for different companies; applications are evaluated case by case
the number of hosts and telemetry events may be limited; the programme page publishes no figure

limits_note: The monitored infrastructure and applications must directly support the project, so instances of an open source project run for other uses are out of scope. Recipients are asked to let the community know how they use Datadog.
binding_note: At least 5 regular contributors and at least 2 maintainers at different companies are required, so a project with one maintainer cannot apply.

identity_cost.detail: The application form requires full name, email, project name, project website or repository, an open source licence and a description, with no card or phone field; eligibility rests on the project's team (at least 5 regular contributors and at least 2 maintainers who work for different companies), which a single maintainer cannot meet.

reliability_note: recipients date from 2016 (the Apache Software Foundation, one of the first) and 2017 (the Python Software Foundation); the programme page names no enforcement past its host and telemetry limits
confidence_note: The conditions, the application form and the limits wording are documented on the programme page; which products an accepted account includes is reported by one recipient project, and the host and event limits set for an accepted project are unverified: behind an application.

The self-serve Free tier is a different offer, recorded as dev-services/datadog: the open source programme is applied for and evaluated case by case, and is open only to a project with regular contributors and maintainers at two or more companies.
